:::{#thm-triangle-inequality}
#### Triangle inequality

For any $\vecf{x}, \vecf{y} \in \reals^p$,

$$
\norm{\vecf{x} + \vecf{y}} \le \norm{\vecf{x}} + \norm{\vecf{y}}.
$$

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\norm{\vecf{x} + \vecf{y}}^2
&= \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 + 2\,(\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}) + \norm{\vecf{y}}^2
&& \text{(@thm-norm-sum-square)}
\\
&\le \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 + 2\,\abs{\vecf{x} \cdot \vecf{y}} + \norm{\vecf{y}}^2
&& \text{(a number is at most its absolute value)}
\\
&\le \norm{\vecf{x}}^2 + 2\,\norm{\vecf{x}}\,\norm{\vecf{y}} + \norm{\vecf{y}}^2
&& \text{(@thm-cauchy-schwarz)}
\\
&= \paren{\norm{\vecf{x}} + \norm{\vecf{y}}}^2.
&& \text{(expand the square)}
\ea
$$

Both $\norm{\vecf{x} + \vecf{y}}$ and $\norm{\vecf{x}} + \norm{\vecf{y}}$
are nonnegative (@thm-norm-properties),
and for nonnegative numbers $a^2 \le b^2$ implies $a \le b$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-triangle-inequality}
#### Two sides of a triangle are longer than the third

- For $\vecf{x} = (3, 0)$ and $\vecf{y} = (0, 4)$:
  $\norm{\vecf{x} + \vecf{y}} = \norm{(3, 4)} = 5$,
  while $\norm{\vecf{x}} + \norm{\vecf{y}} = 3 + 4 = 7$.
- For $\vecf{x} = (1, 0)$ and $\vecf{y} = (2, 0)$, which point the same way:
  $\norm{(3, 0)} = 3 = 1 + 2$, so equality holds.

:::
